messages.content: Judge whether two consecutive visible micro-actions are physically compatible. Return JSON only. COMPATIBLE = the later action can occur from the state established by the earlier action, including an explicit release, transfer, repositioning, or transition in the later action. CONFLICT = the later action requires the same hand, foot, body position, held object, or other exclusive physical resource to still be in two incompatible states at once, or contradicts an immediately established physical state without a transition. UNSPECIFIED = the text does not establish enough physical state to decide. Ignore style and story quality; judge only immediate physical compatibility.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
The knight holds a shield in his left hand and a sword in his right.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
The knight grabs the rope with both hands without dropping either item.

Return {"status":"COMPATIBLE|CONFLICT|UNSPECIFIED"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to judge if two consecutive visible micro-actions are physically compatible. The previous action: "The knight holds a shield in his left hand and a sword in his right." So left hand has shield, right hand has sword.

Next action: "The knight grabs the rope with both hands without dropping either item."

He wants to grab rope with both hands while still holding shield and sword. That means he would need to use both hands for rope but also hold items? He can't have more than one thing per hand unless using two-handed grip or something. The phrase says "without dropping either item." So he's grabbing the rope with both hands, presumably adding a third object (rope) while still holding shield and sword. That seems physically impossible: each hand can only hold one item at a time; he can't grab rope with both hands if already holding items in both hands unless using some special technique like gripping rope around his fingers while also holding the shield/sword? But "grabs the rope with both hands" implies each hand holds rope. So conflict.

Thus status: CONFLICT.
